sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Florida's homes?
sections.html:
The state holds 10,789,047 housing units as of July 1, 2025, for an estimated 23,462,518 residents, and owners put the middle home at $359,000 across 2020 to 2024 (QuickFacts, Florida).

Growth is brisk. The estimate for mid-2025 sits 8.9 percent above the April 2020 base. Density rose from 350.6 people per square mile in 2010 to 401.4 in 2020 across 53,652.17 square miles of land. New supply keeps arriving too, with 178,297 building permits recorded for 2025.

sections.h2: How many Florida homes are lived in by their owners?
sections.html:
Roughly two in three: 67.6 percent for the 2020 to 2024 period. That leaves about a third of occupied homes to renters. The bureau counts 8,752,810 households averaging 2.51 people.

Residents mostly stay put. About 86.3 percent of people aged one and older had not moved in the prior year. Sellers therefore draw buyers from arrivals as much as from neighbors trading up.

The age mix is notable. Those 65 and older make up 22.8 percent of the population, and 1,327,071 residents are veterans. Both groups connect to homestead benefits described in the state's senior and veteran guides, which shape what a buyer or an heir pays after a sale.

sections.h2: What are typical monthly housing costs in Florida?
sections.html:
Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,959. Owners without one report $673. Renters pay a median gross rent of $1,669. All three come from the 2020 to 2024 survey period.

The spread between the owner figures shows how much of a payment is the loan itself. A paid-off house still carries taxes, insurance and upkeep, so an heir holding a free-and-clear property pays less per month yet faces vacancy risk, repairs and the autumn tax bill.

For comparison, median household income is $74,568 in 2024 dollars, per capita income is $42,609, and 12.0 percent of people are below the poverty line.

sections.h2: What do workers and buyers look like statewide?
sections.html:
Income and rent sit close enough to show pressure on buyers: median gross rent of $1,669 a month eats a visible share of a $74,568 household income. About 59.3 percent of residents 16 and older are in the labor force, and commutes average 28.0 minutes each way.

Other rows describe the buyer pool. Some 34.1 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, 21.9 percent were born abroad, and 30.6 percent of residents five and older use another language at home. A seller benefits from plain, bilingual-friendly paperwork.

Business rows add context: 645,575 employer establishments in 2023, employment near 9,988,508, and 2022 retail sales of $484,218,148,000. These are statewide sums, so check the county or city page in QuickFacts for your own location.

sections.h2: How do transfer taxes and recording charges affect a Florida sale?
sections.html:
Documentary stamp tax applies to the deed. The revenue agency prints a rate of 70 cents for each $100 of consideration everywhere except Miami-Dade, where it is 60 cents plus a 45 cent surtax that skips a document moving only a single-family dwelling. Every party to the document is liable regardless of who agrees to pay (doc stamp page).

The clerk also charges to record. Under s. 28.24(13) that means $5.00 on page one, $4.00 on each later page, a $1.00 and $0.50 trust fund charge, and a $4 per page technology charge (s. 28.24).

Property tax runs on a fixed rhythm: assessment each January 1, bills in November, and discounts that shrink from 4 percent to 1 percent by February.

sections.h2: How does homestead protection split buyers from long-time owners?
sections.html:
It opens a gap. Save Our Homes holds a homestead's assessed value growth to the smaller of 3 percent or CPI, and a sale resets the parcel to just value the next January 1 (pt112). Property without homestead is limited to 10 percent per year, which explains why neighboring houses can carry quite different bills.

  • Read the appraiser's record for assessed and just value.
  • Ask the tax collector about any deferral or installment plan.
  • Check that an owner who moved out has not left a stale exemption.

None of that shows up in a median, so local records beat averages.

sections.h2: Which county offices does a Florida seller deal with?
sections.html:
Florida is divided into 67 counties, and each elects a sheriff, tax collector, property appraiser, supervisor of elections and clerk of the circuit court to four year terms (Senate bill analysis). Three of those offices touch a home sale.

  • The property appraiser sets just value each January, mails the August notice and rules on exemptions.
  • The tax collector bills, collects, takes deferral and installment requests, and sells certificates on unpaid items.
  • The clerk records the deed, collects stamp tax at recording and runs foreclosure and tax deed auctions.

Knowing which door to knock on saves a seller days at closing.

sections.h2: What happens when Florida property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax turns delinquent on April 1, and the tax collector sells certificates on unpaid items by June 1 (state calendar). Bidders compete on the lowest interest rate in quarter percent steps, and the county takes any certificate that finds no bidder at the maximum rate (s. 197.432).

A certificate holder may not demand payment from the owner until two years after April 1 of the issue year, and may apply for a tax deed after that same period. Homeowners considering a quick sale should clear delinquencies first, since a buyer's lender will insist.

sections.h2: What should a seller verify before leaning on statewide averages?
sections.html:
Look at the county, the neighborhood and the house. One state median blends beach condos, inland ranch homes and rural parcels.

County offices hold the facts that set closing costs. The appraiser publishes values, the clerk records deeds and collects stamp tax, and the tax collector sends bills.

QuickFacts does not carry sale price, days on market or sales volume. A local agent or the clerk's recorded sales can fill that gap.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Florida?
faqs.a: $359,000 across 2020 to 2024, based on what owners estimate their homes are worth in the Census survey. It is not a recorded sale price.

faqs.q: What share of Florida homes are owner-occupied?
faqs.a: 67.6 percent for 2020 to 2024. The state has 8,752,810 households averaging 2.51 people.

faqs.q: What does a Florida renter pay?
faqs.a: A median gross rent of $1,669 in the 2020 to 2024 data. Owner costs are $1,959 a month with a mortgage and $673 without.

faqs.q: How many homes does Florida have?
faqs.a: 10,789,047 housing units on July 1, 2025, for a population estimated at 23,462,518.

faqs.q: Do Florida sellers face a deed tax?
faqs.a: Yes, documentary stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 of consideration in most counties. Miami-Dade charges 60 cents plus a 45 cent surtax that a single-family dwelling transfer avoids. The state holds all parties liable.
